Prayer of Aeolus.lead_extra: It is the only craftable source of Anemos, and is crafted from seven {{MCW|Wind Charge|wind charges}} and a {{MCW|Block of Gold|block of gold}}.
Prayer of Aeolus.usage: Anemos applies to swords and sticks, while Wind Burst applies only to {{MCW|Mace|maces}}, so no single item can use both enchantments from one book. Anemos is forbidden on maces. Applying the book to a sword gives Anemos; applying it to a mace gives Wind Burst.
Prayer of Aeolus.trivia: Aeolus is the keeper of the winds in Greek mythology, matching the wind charges in the recipe and the wind-based enchantments.

Prayer of Apollo.lead_extra: It is crafted from four [[Spectral Arrow]]s, three gold ingots and a {{MCW|Disc Fragment|disc fragment}}.
Prayer of Apollo.usage: Impaling applies to tridents and Piercing to crossbows. Both levels are below the vanilla maximums (Impaling V, Piercing IV).
Prayer of Apollo.trivia: Apollo is the Greek god of archery and music, reflected in the arrows and the music disc fragment in the recipe. One of the pack's title-screen splashes reads "Ft. Apollo: Our Fave Problematic King!".<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.10|quote=Ft. Apollo: Our Fave Problematic King!}}</ref>

Prayer of Ares.lead_extra: It is crafted from an iron sword or iron spear, a shield, an iron helmet and a red dye, the arms of a soldier.
Prayer of Ares.usage: Lunge applies to spears and Breach to maces.
Prayer of Ares.trivia: Ares is the Greek god of war.

Prayer of Artemis.lead_extra: It is crafted from four [[Spectral Arrow]]s, three raw porkchops and a [[Silver Bullion]].
Prayer of Artemis.usage: Power applies to bows and Multishot to crossbows. Power II is also available from the Prayer of Exodus [[Ofuda]].
Prayer of Artemis.trivia: Artemis is the Greek goddess of the hunt and of the moon; the recipe pairs arrows and game meat with silver.

Prayer of Cronus.lead_extra: It is crafted from four {{MCW|Sculk|sculk}}, three {{MCW|Echo Shard|echo shards}} and an iron hoe. Swift Sneak and Soul Speed are otherwise found only in [[Ancient City|ancient city]] chests and [[Bastion Remnant|bastions]] or by {{MCW|Bartering|bartering}}.
Prayer of Cronus.usage: Swift Sneak applies to leggings and Soul Speed to boots.
Prayer of Cronus.trivia: Cronus is the Titan of Greek mythology who was later identified with time, and he is often shown with a sickle, represented here by the hoe.

Prayer of Daedalus.lead_extra: It is crafted from a [[Divine Favor]], a diamond pickaxe, a diamond axe, four [[Estus Ash]] and a diamond, and is the only craftable source of Unbreaking III and of Efficiency.
Prayer of Daedalus.usage: Efficiency applies to mining tools, and Unbreaking to any item with durability. The only other source of Efficiency besides loot is the Prayer of The God-King [[Ofuda]] (Efficiency II and Unbreaking I).
Prayer of Daedalus.trivia: Daedalus is the craftsman and inventor of Greek myth, father of Icarus (see [[Elegy of Icarus]]). The developer thanked a contributor in the {{Version|1.12.1-alpha}} release notes with "may you be blessed by Daedalus himself".<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.1-alpha|quote=Thank you, HapppySpud, for your work, and may you be blessed by Daedalus himself}}</ref>

Prayer of Demeter.lead_extra: It is crafted from four golden apples, three blue ice and a golden hoe, and is the only craftable source of Frost Protection.
Prayer of Demeter.usage: Frost Walker applies to boots and Frost Protection to chestplates. Any level of Frost Protection on the chestplate protects from [[freezing water]], so this book is enough for that.
Prayer of Demeter.trivia: Demeter is the Greek goddess of the harvest; her grief for Persephone brings winter in the myth, matching the frost enchantments and the hoe in the recipe.
history: Now counts toward the blessing crafting advancement.

Prayer of Eros.lead_extra: It is crafted from a [[Shakudo Alloy]], four arrows and three [[Estus Ash]].
Prayer of Eros.usage: Silk Touch applies to mining tools. It is exclusive with [[Fortune]] and with the electrum and adamant tool [[intrinsic]]s. [[Shakudo equipment|Shakudo]] tools already have Silk Touch as an intrinsic.
Prayer of Eros.trivia: Eros is the Greek god of love, who strikes with arrows; the "soft touch" of love matches Silk Touch. The pack also has an advancement called "Wings of Eros".

Prayer of Glaucus.ench: {{MCW|Luck of the Sea}} III, {{MCW|Lure}} III and {{MCW|Loyalty}} I
Prayer of Glaucus.lead_extra: It is crafted from three nautilus shells and an azure bluet.
Prayer of Glaucus.usage: Luck of the Sea and Lure apply to [[Fishing Rod|fishing rods]] at their vanilla maximum of III; Loyalty applies to tridents. See [[Fishing]] for how the pack's fishing uses luck.
Prayer of Glaucus.trivia: Glaucus is a fisherman of Greek myth who became a sea god, suiting the fishing enchantments.

Prayer of Lu Ban.lead_extra: It is crafted from a [[Divine Favor]], six diamonds and a {{MCW|Block of Diamond|block of diamond}}, making it one of the two most expensive blessings.
Prayer of Lu Ban.usage: Mending applies to any item with durability. The only other sources are loot and the Prayer of Belial [[Ofuda]]. The book has epic rarity.
Prayer of Lu Ban.trivia: Lu Ban is a Chinese carpenter and engineer, venerated as the patron of builders and craftsmen, fitting an enchantment that keeps tools repaired.

Prayer of Man.lead_extra: It is crafted from four [[Baked Golden Apple]]s, three lapis lazuli and a [[Silver Bullion]], and is the only book that stores a [[Warding]] enchantment.
Prayer of Man.usage: Warding 2 is one of the pack's [[intrinsic]] enchantments, which burns nearby [[undead]]; the warding enchantments are exclusive with each other and with the other alloy intrinsics. The book shows Warding as its glyph (✟) rather than a name. Smite applies to weapons. The book has rare rarity.
Prayer of Man.trivia: Unlike the other prayers, it is not addressed to a deity. Its texture file is named blessing_warding.

Prayer of Midas.lead_extra: It is crafted from an {{MCW|Ominous Bottle|ominous bottle}}, three {{MCW|Block of Gold|blocks of gold}} and four [[Estus Ash]].
Prayer of Midas.usage: Looting applies to swords, spears and shears in the pack. Fortune applies to mining tools, but its maximum level is I in Matcha Flavoured; higher Fortune comes only from [[Electrum equipment|electrum]] tools. The ominous bottle is itself crafted with [[Benzene]].
Prayer of Midas.trivia: King Midas turned everything he touched to gold, fitting enchantments that increase drops.
history: Added.<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.1-alpha|quote=Blessing: Prayer of Midas (Craftable Looting)}}</ref>

Prayer of Paris.lead_extra: It is crafted from seven [[Spectral Arrow]]s and a [[Stable Void]].
Prayer of Paris.trivia: Paris is the Trojan prince who killed Achilles with an arrow.

Prayer of Prometheus.lead_extra: It is crafted from a [[Divine Fragment]], three diamonds and four [[Estus Ash]], and is the cheapest craftable source of Unbreaking.
Prayer of Prometheus.usage: Unbreaking applies to any item with durability. The [[Prayer of Daedalus]] gives Unbreaking III, but costs a full [[Divine Favor]].
Prayer of Prometheus.trivia: Prometheus is the Titan who stole fire for humanity and was punished by the gods. The developer's video names the unbreaking book as a reason the player needs divine fragments.<ref>{{Cite video|quote=If you want to make an unbreaking book, Bedrock Busters, Crystal Hearts, or netherite, you need that fragment.}}</ref>
history: Now gives Unbreaking II.<ref>{{Cite changelog|0.4-alpha|quote=Buffed Prometheus' Prayer to unbreaking II}}</ref>

Prayer of St. Clement.lead_extra: It is crafted from a pair of leather boots, two wool of any color and two [[Obol]]s.
Prayer of St. Clement.usage: Trailblaze applies to boots and speeds the wearer up on paths, gravel, coarse dirt and mud bricks. Level III is the maximum. The Prayer of Exodus [[Ofuda]] also gives Trailblaze III.
Prayer of St. Clement.trivia: Saint Clement is traditionally the patron saint of hatters and felt makers; legend credits him with discovering felt by lining his sandals with wool, as the recipe lines boots with wool. The enchantment's internal id is still traversal.
history: Now works.<ref>{{Cite changelog|0.5-alpha|quote=St. Clement's Prayer now works}}</ref>

Prayer of Talos.lead_extra: It is crafted from seven {{MCW|Block of Iron|blocks of iron}} and a [[Steel Alloy]], and has rare rarity.
Prayer of Talos.usage: Density applies to maces, Knockback to melee weapons and Punch to bows. Knockback II and Punch II are the vanilla maximums.
Prayer of Talos.trivia: Talos is the bronze giant of Greek myth who guarded Crete, hence the metal-heavy recipe.

Prayer of The Light.lead_extra: It is crafted from three [[Silver Bullion]], four [[Estus Ash]] and a gold ingot.
Prayer of The Light.usage: Smite applies to weapons and Channeling to tridents. Smite IV is the highest Smite available from a blessing; the [[Prayer of Man]] gives Smite II.
Prayer of The Light.trivia: Its internal name is god_king, and it was called the "Prayer of God-King" until {{Version|1.10}}, when the display name changed to "Prayer of The Light" and "Prayer of The God-King" went to the Avesta [[Ofuda]].{{Cite changelog|1.10|quote=Prayer of God-King, is still labeled as such in the Lang (to preserve update consistency) however the translation was changed to "Prayer of The Light" the Prayer of Ahura Mazda was changed to "Prayer of the God-King"}}
history: Renamed from Prayer of God-King. Recipe made cheaper.

Prayer of Will.lead_extra: It is crafted from four [[Stable Void]]s.
Prayer of Will.usage: Reach applies to chestplates and adds 2 blocks of block interaction range. Level I is the only level any source gives, although the enchantment goes up to III.
Prayer of Will.trivia: Its lore line is item.kleispack.blessing.will in the language file.

Prayer of Yama.lead_extra: It is crafted from four {{MCW|Fire Charge|fire charges}} and four gold ingots.
Prayer of Yama.usage: Flame applies to bows, Fire Aspect to swords and Fire Protection to armor. Applying the book to one item gives only the enchantments that item supports.
Prayer of Yama.trivia: Yama is the god of death in Hindu and Buddhist tradition, ruler of the underworld; the pack calls its Nether "[[Hell]]".

Prayer of Yamm.ench: {{MCW|Depth Strider}} II, {{MCW|Riptide}} I, {{MCW|Aqua Affinity}} and {{MCW|Respiration}} II
Prayer of Yamm.lead_extra: It is crafted from four nautilus shells, and stores four enchantments, more than any other blessing.
Prayer of Yamm.usage: Depth Strider applies to boots, Riptide to tridents, and Aqua Affinity and Respiration to helmets.
Prayer of Yamm.trivia: Yamm is the Canaanite god of the sea.

Elegy of Arachnae.lead_extra: It is crafted from four spider eyes, and is the only blessing that gives an enchantment at its vanilla maximum level of V.
Elegy of Arachnae.usage: Bane of Arthropods applies to weapons. It is exclusive with Sharpness, Smite and [[Slaughter]].
Elegy of Arachnae.trivia: Arachne is the weaver of Greek myth whom Athena turned into a spider. The pack spells the name "Arachnae", and the recipe file is spelled bane_of_arthopods.

Elegy of Hyacinthus.lead_extra: It is crafted from four wind charges, three feathers and a [[Hyacinth]].
Elegy of Hyacinthus.usage: Zephyr applies to boots. At level I, sneaking gives Jump Boost VII. Levels II and III, which add Slow Falling and a charged updraft, have no source in survival: no recipe, trade or loot gives them.
Elegy of Hyacinthus.trivia: In Greek myth, Hyacinthus was loved by Apollo and by Zephyrus, the west wind, and the hyacinth flower grew from his blood when he died. The recipe uses a [[hyacinth]] (the pack's name for the allium) and wind charges.

Elegy of Icarus.lead_extra: It is crafted from four wind charges, three feathers and a [[Wax]].
Elegy of Icarus.usage: Feather Falling applies to boots. The pack doubles its effect, so Feather Falling II reduces fall damage by 48%.
Elegy of Icarus.trivia: Icarus flew on wings of feathers and wax made by his father Daedalus (see [[Prayer of Daedalus]]) and fell when the sun melted the wax, which the recipe's feathers and wax refer to. The pack has an advancement called "Icarus' Folly".
history: Now gives Feather Falling II.<ref>{{Cite changelog|0.5-alpha|quote=Buffed Icarus' prayer to feather falling II}}</ref>
